name: Whole rockfish
tile_uses: The weekend meal, fish tacos, a weeknight instead of salmon
why_now: Rockfish is the local fish that gets more reliable as the water cools in fall: dozens of species, all mild and firm, and usually cheaper than anything flown in. Bought whole, it's the easiest good fish dinner there is — and the one most people have never cooked. This is the month to swap it in for salmon.
how_to_choose: Clear, bright, slightly bulging eyes; cloudy or sunken means it's been sitting
Bright red gills under the flap; brown means old
Firm flesh that springs back when pressed
It should smell like the ocean, not like fish
Ask the counter to scale and gut it — they will, and it takes them two minutes
buy_this_much: One fish, 2–3 lbs, feeds two or three. For a weeknight, 1 lb of fillets feeds two.
price_note: Usually $6–10 a pound whole, less than salmon fillets. Asian markets and the harbor's weekend fish market sell it whole; supermarkets more often sell fillets, sometimes labeled rock cod or Pacific snapper.

flavor_paths.name: Whole, roasted hot
flavor_paths.description: Slashed, salted, lemon inside, 450°F. The weekend meal.

flavor_paths.name: Fillets, pan-seared
flavor_paths.description: Skin side down, three minutes a side. A weeknight in place of salmon.

flavor_paths.name: Flaked
flavor_paths.description: Into tacos with arugula, pomegranate, and lime.

weekday_uses: Fillets pan-seared, over rice, with a spoonful of ajvar
Flaked into tacos with arugula and pomegranate
Leftovers from the whole fish, cold, with lemon and olive oil on toast
In place of salmon in anything you already make
weekend_use: Roasted whole at 450°F with lemon, beside the October salad. The weekend meal.
storage: Cook it the day you buy it, or the next. Keep it in the coldest part of the fridge on a plate, loosely covered, ideally over a bag of ice.
one_thing_to_learn: A whole fish is more forgiving than a fillet. The bone slows the heat and the skin holds in moisture, so the window between done and overdone is minutes, not seconds. To check, push a thin knife into the thickest part near the spine: if the flesh is opaque and pulls away from the bone, it's done.
